Piston skirt relief, an illustrative modelling decision with no source for the real piston (20 Oct 2026): each of the six pistons has a stepped relief cut into the skirt on the flank that faces the neighbouring crank bay (22 x 27 x 103 mm for the big-end hardware plus a 9.4 x 51 x 116 mm step for the counterweights; 16.1 cm3, 4.5 % of the piston, removed). The two opposed pistons of a bay reach bottom dead centre together and the reconstruction's bay pitch is 56 mm, so the neighbour rod's big end, the crank pin and the counterweights would otherwise pass through the skirt. The real piston skirt, crank pin width and bay pitch are not in the project sources; the sizes are the swept overlaps plus about 1.5 mm, leaving 3.0 mm of web to the lowest ring groove and the pin boss. One parameterised cut in cad_pipeline/gtsio_core.py (piston_relief_*); docs/r10-cycle-overlap-root-causes.md.
